newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Top banker says Bangladesh banking not in danger.
newsitem.headline: Top banker says Bangladesh banking not in danger.

text.p: The head of Bangladesh's largest state-owned commercial bank said on Friday the country's banking system was not in mortal crisis.
"(The) present position of the banks (in Bangladesh) are generally not bad," Ibrahim Khaled, Managing Director of Sonali Bank, said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
He said only two banks in the private sector were causing concern and all other banks, including the state-owned ones, were showing "acceptable results".

Bangladesh's central bank Governor, Lutfar Rahman Sarkar, triggered an alarm on Wednesday when a bank press release quoted him as saying the country's banking sector was "on the verge of collapse" because of a huge accumulation of bad debt.
Sarkar said the banking sector was grappling with 130 billion taka ($3 billion) of defaulted loans.
Khaled said the Governor had been misquoted.

"I was present at the meeting (where Sarkar explained the banks' woes). He did not use such words (like collapse) as I could hear. What he said was that the amount of classified loans is so high that it is a concern," Khaled said.
Sarkar was not available for comment.
Khaled said the amount of the bad loans was looking large due to the existing "rigid" way of loan classification that Bangladeshi banks are following under on-going reforms.
He said the burden of classified loans with state-owned banks was about 30 percent of their total advances while the rate is 40 percent in the case of private banks. REUTER
